newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soy basis prices fall on high nearby offer.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soy basis prices fall on high nearby offer.

text.p: Brazilian soymeal basis prices for July shipment fell sharply and soybeans tumbled in sympathy amid talk of heavy nearby supply and rumors that China may have cancelled some cargoes of soymeal, traders said.
July soymeal was being offered at a discount of $42 per tonne Wednesday, up from $29 the previous session. Soybeans were being offered at a discount of $0.40 per bushel, up from $0.15 Tuesday.

"There is a very good offer of pellets for nearby positions in Brazil and Argentina," said David Brew, trader at Brasoja. "This is increasing the discount for pellets...and beans are collapsing in sympathy."

Traders were split about talk China cancelled some shipments of Brazilian soymeal. Some said this was partly to blame for the rise in discounts, but several large international trading firms said they hadn't heard anything about it.
"China is cancelling some purchases because they have a severe drop in basis prices everywhere," said a soymeal trader.

"The overall situation is that the price of soybeans has been very high for a long time and at one stage you start to lose demand," he said. "It shows itself in cancelling in China and the basis levels coming off substantially in Argentina and then following in Brazil."

Because of low supply for old crop months in the U.S., Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) prices for the July contract were remaining high and not accurately reflecting the situation in the rest of the world, the trader said.
"Chicago is no longer faithfully representing the situation," he said, concluding, "The premium has to compensate for this effect."
The weak basis levels were likely to trigger some fund liquidation in old crop soymeal and beans, said Michael McDougall, director of commodities futures at Fimat Futures.
McDougall said he had not heard talk of the China cancellations. "Maybe the market is overbought a little bit," he said.
Traders here could not confirm reports out of Seoul that South Korea's Korea Feed Association bought 30,000 to 35,000 tonnes Brazilian soymeal for August-September shipment.
"Generally speaking, it's a good deal to buy now," opined the soymeal trader.
But Brew said that with prices falling, many buyers would want to hold off on purchases until they were sure the market had bottomed.
